text:
**Delete Account & Data** is at the very bottom of the **Settings** tab, below
Sign Out, in red.

It does what it says. This page exists so you know exactly what you are agreeing
to before you tap it.

Deleting your account is permanent. Your songs, recordings, concepts and
projects are removed, and there is no undo and no grace period. If you only
want to stop using the app on this device, [sign out](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/signing-in/)
instead.
description: How to delete your account and everything in it, and what happens to shared songs when you do.
platformNote: The web app has no way to delete your account. Delete it from the iOS app, or email us from the address at the foot of this page. Deleting removes your songs on the web too, since it is one account. If you subscribed on the web, cancel in the web app's Settings first.

heading: What it asks you
text:
The app checks three times, in three different ways, because the action cannot
be taken back.

1. **Are you sure?** The alert above, which says plainly that it is
   irreversible.
2. **Confirm deletion.** A second alert warning that your song data will be
   unrecoverable.
3. **Prove it is you.** A sign-in sheet, because deleting an account is not
   something a borrowed phone should be able to do.

Only after all three does anything happen. Cancel is available at every step.
description: How to delete your account and everything in it, and what happens to shared songs when you do.
platformNote: The web app has no way to delete your account. Delete it from the iOS app, or email us from the address at the foot of this page. Deleting removes your songs on the web too, since it is one account. If you subscribed on the web, cancel in the web app's Settings first.

heading: While it runs
text:
A full-screen progress view counts through the work: fetching your songs,
deleting them one by one, cleaning up invitations, then your user data, then
the account itself.

It asks you not to close the app while this happens, and that is worth
honouring. Stopping halfway leaves some of it done.

heading: What happens to shared songs
text:
Songs you own that have co-writers on them do not vanish from those co-writers.
Each of them keeps a personal copy under a new title, so the work they did
survives. They are told the collaboration ended.

Songs somebody else owns are unaffected. You simply stop being on them.

heading: What is not deleted
text:
Your subscription. Deleting your account does not cancel it, whether you
bought Pro in the iOS app or on the web.

Cancel first, where you subscribed: the App Store, under your Apple ID, for a
subscription bought in the app, or Settings in the web app for one bought on
the web. See [Plans and Pro](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/plans/).

Lyric sheets you created stay reachable at their links unless you delete them
first, because they are published pages rather than account data. If you have
shared sheets you want taken down, delete them from each song before you delete
the account. See [Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/).

text:
Lyric Genie is free to use. Pro adds the AI writing tools and lifts the caps on
rhymes and recording.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: One plan, both apps
text:
Pro belongs to your account, not to a device. Subscribe in the web app or in
the iOS app, and the same plan applies on the web, your iPhone and your iPad.
You only ever need one subscription.

New to Pro? The first 14 days are free, whichever app you start in. The trial
is only offered once per account, so if you have had one before, Pro starts
straight away.

Web app:
**Upgrade** is in **Settings**, beside your plan, and the same dialog opens
when you run out of free AI calls. Pick yearly or monthly and click
**Continue to checkout**. Payment is handled by Stripe, and you come back to
Settings once it is done. Pro switches on a moment later.

**Usage & Stats** in Settings shows your recording storage and AI use against
the limits below.

iPhone and iPad app:
Subscribe from **Pro Subscription** in **Settings**, or from any upgrade
screen. Payment goes through your Apple ID.

If you already have Pro from the web, the Pro screen says so and links to the
web app's Settings, where that subscription is managed. It does not offer you a
second one.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: What Pro adds
text:
| Feature | Free | Pro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [In-line suggestions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/inline-suggestions/) | Try | Yes |
| [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) | Try | Yes |
| Smart dictionaries | Try | Yes |
| AI song titles | Try | Yes |
| [Song concepts and Spark](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/song-wizard/) | Try | Yes |
| [Syllable control](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/syllables/) | Try | Yes |
| AI calls | {{limit.ai.freeCalls}} in total | {{limit.ai.proMonthly}} a month |
| Quick AI calls (suggestions, rhyme picks) | {{limit.ai.freeCallsLowCost}} in total | {{limit.ai.proMonthlyLowCost}} a month |
| [Rhyme lookups](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/rhymes/) | {{limit.rhymes.freeDaily}} a day | Unlimited |
| Voice recording | {{limit.recording.freeTotal}} in total | {{limit.recording.proTotal}} in total |
| Longest single recording or import | {{limit.recording.freePerItem}} | {{limit.recording.proPerItem}} |
| Original files (keep imported audio as uploaded) | No | Yes |
| Genie chat (web) | Uses your AI calls | 1,000 messages a month |
| Sessions (web) (coming soon) | Join a Pro writer's | Start and join |

"Try" means the free plan includes {{limit.ai.freeCalls}} of the larger AI
calls and {{limit.ai.freeCallsLowCost}} of the lighter ones, so every AI feature
above can be tried before paying. Pro raises that to {{limit.ai.proMonthly}} and
{{limit.ai.proMonthlyLowCost}} a month, reset on the 1st. See
[Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: Original files
text:
When you import audio, Lyric Genie converts it to M4A so it plays everywhere.
On Pro it also keeps the file exactly as you uploaded it, a WAV stays a WAV,
and you can download it again from the take's menu with **Download Original**.

Each original can be up to 250 MB, and you can keep 10 GB of them in total.
**Original Files** in Settings lists them, shows the space they use, and lets
you download or delete them. On a shared song, co-writers can download your
originals too (in the web app).

If Pro ends, your originals are kept for 30 days and you get an email before
they go. Come back to Pro inside that window and nothing is deleted. Your
converted recordings are never affected.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: What is free, and stays free
text:
Three things people assume are paid, and are not.

- **[Collaboration](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/).** Inviting co-writers, tabs,
  sending lines, the Master tab. All of it.
- **[Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/).** Making them and sharing them.
- **Recordings linked to lyrics.** Tying a take to particular words.

Also free: writing, arranging, sections, [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/),
importing, and the Scratchpad.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: How the limits actually work
text:
**Rhyme lookups** count distinct words per calendar day. Looking up a word you
already looked up today is free and does not count again, so revisiting your
own work never costs you anything. A counter appears once you are running low.

**Recording storage** is a total, not a monthly allowance. Deleting old
recordings gives the space back.

**Longest recording** applies per item, to both what you record and what you
import. A long file is refused with its length in the message, rather than
silently truncated.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: When you are running out of recording space (iPhone and iPad)
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The app warns you before you hit the wall rather than after. At around
ninety per cent of your total it says **You're running low on storage**, with
how many minutes you have used and how many you have.

At the cap it says **Storage limit reached** with the same numbers. Both alerts
carry an **Upgrade to Pro** button beside **OK**, so the upgrade is right there
if that is what you want. Deleting recordings you no longer need also works,
and gives the space back immediately.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: Have a code? (web)
text:
Web app:
If someone gave you a Lyric Genie code, click **Have a code?** in the upgrade
dialog, type it, and continue to checkout. A code that makes Pro free skips the
trial and does not ask for a card. Each code works once. If it has already been
used, the dialog says so.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: Cancelling: do it where you subscribed
text:
A subscription can only be cancelled by whoever bills it.

- **Subscribed on the web** (Stripe): cancel in the web app's Settings.
- **Subscribed in the iOS app** (Apple): cancel in your Apple ID's
  subscriptions, on an iPhone, iPad or Mac.

Either way, you keep Pro until the end of the period you have paid for, and
nothing is deleted when it ends. You go back to the free plan's limits. The one
exception is [original files](#original-files), which are kept for 30 days and
then removed.

Deleting your Lyric Genie account does **not** cancel your subscription, on
either store. Cancel first, then delete. See
[Deleting your account](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/deleting/).

Web app:
**If you subscribed on the web**, open **Settings**. Under your plan, click
**Cancel subscription** and confirm on the page that opens. Settings then says
**Cancelled, Pro until** and the date. Changed your mind? **Resume** is in the
same place until that date. **Manage** opens the same page for switching
between monthly and yearly, changing your card, or downloading invoices.

**If you subscribed in the iOS app**, Settings says **Billed through the App
Store** and offers **Manage in App Store**. Cancel from an Apple device, or
follow Apple's steps, which Settings links to. The web app cannot cancel an
Apple subscription.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: Starting a trial (iPhone and iPad)
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The Pro screen offers a free trial, then a monthly price, with an annual option
that works out cheaper per month. Nothing is charged until the trial ends.

If you have used a trial on this Apple ID before, the app says so and offers
the subscription without one.
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: Cancelling an App Store subscription (iPhone and iPad)
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
**There is no cancel button inside the iOS app, and there cannot be.** A
subscription bought in the app is billed by Apple, and only Apple can stop it.
That is the same for every app on the App Store. If you subscribed on the web
instead, cancel in the web app's Settings.

To cancel an App Store subscription, on the iPhone or iPad you subscribed on:

1. Open the **Settings** app, the grey one with the gears, not Lyric Genie.
2. Tap **your name** at the very top.
3. Tap **Subscriptions**.
4. Tap **Lyric Genie**.
5. Tap **Cancel Subscription**, and confirm.

The App Store app gets you to the same place: tap your photo in the top right,
then **Subscriptions**.

**Cancelling does not end Pro straight away.** You keep it until the end of the

period you have already paid for, and you are not charged again. Nothing is

deleted when it lapses, either: your songs, recordings and lyric sheets all

stay. You go back to the free plan's limits.

iPhone and iPad app:
If you cannot find Lyric Genie in that list, either you subscribed on the web,
or you are signed in to a different Apple ID from the one that bought it. An
App Store subscription belongs to an Apple ID, not to your Lyric Genie account.

Deleting your Lyric Genie account does **not** cancel your subscription. They

are two separate things with two separate owners, so cancel first and delete

second. See [Deleting your account](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/deleting/).
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

heading: If you cancelled and changed your mind (iPhone and iPad)
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Cancelling a subscription does not switch Pro off straight away. It runs to the
end of the period you paid for, and during that window the Pro screen says your
subscription is **set to expire** rather than thanking you for subscribing.

That is when **Resume Subscription** appears. It opens Apple's own subscription
sheet, which is the only place auto-renew can be turned back on. **Change Plan**
is beside it if you want to move between monthly and annual instead.

Once the period actually ends, the screen goes back to the ordinary upgrade
offer.

There is no Restore Purchases button. Subscriptions restore themselves from

your Apple ID, so if Pro is not showing after reinstalling, check you are signed

into the same Apple ID rather than looking for a restore control.

The numbers on this page are generated from the app's own configuration, so
they are what your copy of the app is actually enforcing. See also
[Plan limits](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/reference/limits/).
description: What the free plan includes, what Pro adds, and which limits govern what.

text:
Web app:
The web app has no separate Preferences screen. Its writing switches are in the
**Editor** section of **Settings**, and they are shared with the iOS app, so
changing one changes it on both. The Editor section also has two Genie
switches that are web-only: **Floating Genie** and **Genie can chime in**. **Default Tab** and the two email switches are
iOS only.

Preferences is the small set of switches that change how the app behaves for
you.

iPhone and iPad app:
Reach it from **Settings**, or from the ⋯ menu inside
[the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/).
description: Which tab opens, whether suggestions appear as you write, the serif font, and what email you get.

heading: App behaviour (iPhone and iPad)
text:
**Default Tab** decides where the app opens: **Start** or **Songs**.

Start is the launch pad, with the four big buttons and your latest songs. Songs
is the full list. If you mostly return to work in progress rather than begin
something new, Songs saves you a tap every time.
description: Which tab opens, whether suggestions appear as you write, the serif font, and what email you get.

heading: Song editor
text:
**In-line Suggestions** offers a line at your cursor after a pause. It has its
own page, including what happens when you do not have AI access. See
[In-line suggestions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/inline-suggestions/).

**Serif Lyric Font** (on the web, **Lyric font**, a choice between Sans and Serif) sets your lyrics and titles in Academico, a serif face,
instead of the default. The label itself is rendered in the serif so you can
see what you are choosing before you choose it.

Worth trying even if you think you do not care. Some writers find a serif reads
more like a page and less like a form, which changes how the words land.
description: Which tab opens, whether suggestions appear as you write, the serif font, and what email you get.

heading: Communications (iPhone and iPad)
text:
Two switches, both about email rather than the app.

| Switch | What it sends |
| --- | --- |
| **Email Updates** | Tips, updates and occasional promotions. |
| **Monthly Recap** | A summary of what you wrote that month. |

iPhone and iPad app:
Push notifications are separate and live in the iOS Settings app under Lyric
Genie, because they are a system permission rather than an app preference. What
arrives in the app's own bell is covered in
[Notifications](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/notifications/).
description: Which tab opens, whether suggestions appear as you write, the serif font, and what email you get.

text:
Your profile is two things at once: the name co-writers see, and the paperwork
that goes on a lyric sheet.

iPhone and iPad app:
Open it by tapping your name at the top of **Settings**.

Web app:
Open it by clicking **Profile** at the top of **Settings**, which you reach from
the menu under your avatar.
description: Your display name, and the writer credits that pre-fill every lyric sheet you make.

heading: Identity
text:
**Display Name** is how you appear on a
[collaborator tab](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/tabs/) and in a co-writer's mailbox. Up to
eighteen characters, with a counter under the field.

This is your name, not your artist name, unless they are the same thing.
description: Your display name, and the writer credits that pre-fill every lyric sheet you make.

heading: Photo (web)
text:
Web app:
The web profile also has a **Photo**, which your co-writers see on shared songs.
Upload one, use your Google photo, or remove it.

When you choose a photo, **Position your photo** opens before anything is
saved. Drag the photo to move it and use the zoom slider to fit it in the
circle. Small previews show it at the sizes your co-writers will see. Click
**Save photo** to use it.

**Use my Google photo** is offered when you signed in with Google, and also
when your account has a Google sign-in linked to it, even if you signed in
another way this time.

Your photo shows on the **Profile** row in Settings and on your avatar at the
top right of the page. When a co-writer changes their photo, the new one shows
up straight away, without you reloading.
description: Your display name, and the writer credits that pre-fill every lyric sheet you make.

heading: Writer profile
text:
These are the details a publisher, a PRO or a split sheet expects. Fill them in
once and every [lyric sheet](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/) you make starts with them
already in place.

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Legal Name** | Your full legal name, as it appears on a contract. Not your artist name. |
| **Writer IPI #** | Your Interested Party Information number, the identifier your PRO knows you by. |
| **Publisher** | Your publisher, if you have one. |
| **Publisher IPI #** | Their number. |
| **PRO Affiliation** | ASCAP, BMI, SESAC, SOCAN, PRS, APRA, or Other. |
| **PRO Name** | Only appears when you choose Other. |
| **Contact Email** | Where business enquiries should go. |

Worth doing before you need it. The moment you want a lyric sheet is usually
the moment somebody has asked for one, and hunting down an IPI number is not
what you want to be doing then.

Nothing here is required. A lyric sheet works with a name alone. The rest is
for when a song is being registered or pitched.
description: Your display name, and the writer credits that pre-fill every lyric sheet you make.

text:
Lyric Genie has two ways in: **Continue with Google** and **Continue with
Apple**. That is the whole list.

There is no email and password option, and no separate account to create. You
pick one of the two and you are in.

This surprises people who expect a sign-up form. There is not one, and you have
not missed a step. Choosing Google or Apple the first time creates your account.
description: Lyric Genie signs in with Google or Apple. There is no password to remember, and signing in is what makes syncing work.

heading: One account, both apps
text:
Web app:
The web app uses the same two buttons, and the same accounts, as the iOS app.
Sign in with the Google or Apple account you use on your iPhone and you see the
same songs, recordings, concepts and projects. **Continue with Google** and
**Continue with Apple** each open a small sign-in window, so allow pop-ups for
the site if nothing appears.

iPhone and iPad app:
Signing in to the web app at app.lyricgenie.app with the same Google or Apple
account shows you the same library there.
description: Lyric Genie signs in with Google or Apple. There is no password to remember, and signing in is what makes syncing work.

heading: Why it matters
text:
Signing in is what makes your work sync. Your songs, recordings, concepts and
projects live with your account, so they appear on any device you sign in on,
and they survive reinstalling the app.

If you are not signed in, you are not syncing. That is the single sentence
worth remembering.
description: Lyric Genie signs in with Google or Apple. There is no password to remember, and signing in is what makes syncing work.

heading: Use the same one every time
text:
Google and Apple are separate accounts as far as Lyric Genie is concerned. If
you signed in with Google the first time and later tap **Continue with Apple**,
you get a new, empty account rather than your songs.

If your library looks empty on a device you have used before, that is almost
always the reason. Sign out and back in with the other one.

If you cannot remember which you used, the answer is on the **Settings** tab
(page, on the web). Your email address is under your name.
description: Lyric Genie signs in with Google or Apple. There is no password to remember, and signing in is what makes syncing work.

heading: When it will not work
text:
Sign-in problems show a message saying what went wrong. The usual causes are:

- **No network.** Both methods have to reach their provider.
- **The sheet was dismissed** before it finished. Tapping outside the Google or
  Apple panel cancels it. On the web, closing the sign-in window or blocking
  pop-ups does the same.

If a message mentions the build being configured incorrectly, that is not
something you can fix from your side. It is worth an email.
description: Lyric Genie signs in with Google or Apple. There is no password to remember, and signing in is what makes syncing work.

heading: Signing out
text:
**Sign Out** is at the bottom of Settings, and on the web it is also in the avatar
menu in the top bar. On iOS it asks before it does anything.

Signing out does not delete anything. Your work stays on your account and comes
back when you sign in again. That is different from
[deleting your account](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/deleting/), which does not.
description: Lyric Genie signs in with Google or Apple. There is no password to remember, and signing in is what makes syncing work.

text:
Every shared song has a chat for the people writing it. Use it to ask about a
line, agree what the chorus is about, share a rough take, or leave a message for
whoever opens the song next.

Only the song's writers see it. Genie does not read it, so it is not the place
to ask Genie something. For that, see [Genie chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/).

The chat needs the latest version of the iPhone app.
description: Talk a shared song through with your co-writers, right beside the lyrics. Send recordings, photos and lines of lyrics without leaving the song.

heading: Finding the chat
text:
A solo song has no chat. It appears once you invite someone. See
[Inviting a co-writer](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/).

iPhone and iPad app:
On a shared song, the **Chat** button (two speech bubbles) is on
the right of the editor's toolbar. A red number on it counts unread messages,
plus any lines a co-writer sent you that you have not answered yet.

The chat opens as a sheet over the bottom half of the screen. Drag it up for
more room. The lyrics stay where they are behind it, so you can keep reading
and writing while it is open. **Done** closes it.

Web app:
On a shared song, **Chat** is a section of the left panel, near
**Collaborators**. On a computer it also has an icon in the column of icons on
the left edge of the window.

- **The expand button** on the section's header, or the icon, opens the chat on
  its own at the full height of the panel.
- **The bar under the message box** sets how tall the chat is inside the
  panel. Drag it up or down. Double-click it to put it back to its usual height.
description: Talk a shared song through with your co-writers, right beside the lyrics. Send recordings, photos and lines of lyrics without leaving the song.

heading: Sending messages
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Type in **Message your co-writers** and tap the arrow to send.

Web app:
Type in **Message co-writers** and press **Enter** to send. Press **Shift**
**Enter** for a new line in the same message. The smiley button beside the box
adds an emoji.

Your messages sit on the right. Your co-writers' sit on the left, with their
name and avatar in their tab colour.

While a co-writer is typing a message, the chat says so under the messages, and
the Collaborators list shows **Typing in chat…** beside their name.

If you have scrolled up to read older messages when new ones arrive, a **New
messages** button appears. Click or tap it to jump to the bottom.
description: Talk a shared song through with your co-writers, right beside the lyrics. Send recordings, photos and lines of lyrics without leaving the song.

heading: Sending a recording or a photo
text:
You can attach up to five things to one message: recordings, photos, or a mix.
Whatever you type goes with them as a caption.

iPhone and iPad app:
Tap the **+** beside the message box and choose:

| Option | What it attaches |
| --- | --- |
| **Photo Library** | A photo from your library. |
| **Audio or Photo File** | An audio file or a picture from Files. |
| **Song Recording** | A take already on this song. |

Web app:
Click the paperclip beside the message box to pick audio files or photos. You
can also drag files onto the chat, or paste a picture.

To share a take that is already on the song, open its ⋯ menu in the
**Recordings** section and choose **Send to Chat**. It goes into the message box
ready to send.

Each attachment shows above the message box while it uploads. The × on one
removes it. Anything you remove, or leave unsent, is thrown away.

**Audio joins the song's Recordings.** A new audio file you send is added to the
song's recordings as your take, so it is there for everyone after the chat has
scrolled away. In the chat it shows as a card you can play. If the take is later
deleted from Recordings, the card says **This recording was deleted**. Audio
files follow the same rules as importing one, including your plan's length
limit. See [Recordings in a song](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/recordings/).

**Photos stay in the chat.** They are scaled down to a sensible size and do not
go anywhere else. Click or tap one to see it full size.

iPhone and iPad app:
In the full-size view, pinch or double-tap to zoom. The share button saves the
photo or sends it on.

Web app:
In the full-size view, the download button saves the photo to your computer.

Pro:
On Pro, an audio file sent in the chat is also kept exactly as you sent it, the
same as an import. See [Original files](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/objects/recordings/#original-files).
description: Talk a shared song through with your co-writers, right beside the lyrics. Send recordings, photos and lines of lyrics without leaving the song.

heading: Lines a co-writer sends you
text:
When a co-writer sends you lines of lyrics, they arrive in the chat as a card:
**Sam sent you 4 lines**, with the lines underneath.

- **Add to my lyrics** puts them at the end of your own tab.
- **Decline** turns them down, and the sender sees that.

Lines you send show the same way on your side, **You sent 4 lines to Sam**, with
what happened to them: **Waiting**, **Added**, **Declined** or **Expired**. See
[Sending lines to a co-writer](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/).
description: Talk a shared song through with your co-writers, right beside the lyrics. Send recordings, photos and lines of lyrics without leaving the song.

heading: Copying and deleting a message
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Touch and hold a message for **Copy**. On your own messages the same menu has
**Delete**.

Web app:
Point at one of your own messages and click the bin beside it.

A deleted message goes for everyone. You can only delete your own messages.
Deleting a message with photos deletes the photos too. A recording it carried
stays in the song's Recordings.
description: Talk a shared song through with your co-writers, right beside the lyrics. Send recordings, photos and lines of lyrics without leaving the song.

heading: New messages
text:
Web app:
A red dot on the **Chat** heading, and on its icon in the left column, means
there are messages you have not read. Reading the chat clears it.

Messages also show on your [Songs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/songs/) list: a shared song shows a
chat bubble with a red number for unread messages, which clears when you read
the chat.

A co-writer who is not in the song when you send a message gets a **new
message** notification in the bell. Opening it takes them straight to the
song's chat. See [Notifications](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/notifications/). There are no
iPhone push notifications for chat yet.

[Search](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/search/) looks through every song's chat, so you can find a
message without remembering which song it was in.
description: Talk a shared song through with your co-writers, right beside the lyrics. Send recordings, photos and lines of lyrics without leaving the song.

text:
Collaboration in Lyric Genie works on invite codes. You generate one, your
co-writer types it in, and the song appears in their app with both of you on
it.

Nothing is emailed. The screen is called Add Collaborator, so people expect an
email to go out, and it does not.

On the web, an invite code is still the way to add someone new. But if you have
written with someone before, the web also lets you pick them from a list and
sends them an invitation by email. See below.

Collaboration is on the free plan. So are lyric sheets and recordings linked to
lyrics. You do not need Pro to write with someone.
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

heading: Sending an invite
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Open the song, tap **Collaborators** in the toolbar, then
**Add Collaborator**.

Web app:
Open the song and find the **Collaborators** section of the left panel (at the
top, once the song is shared). Click **Invite a co-writer**, or **Another invite** if you
have made one already. A picker titled **Invite Co-writers** opens. Tick what you
want and click **Invite**:

- **New co-writer** gets an invite code to share with anyone.
- **Previous co-writers** lists people you have shared songs with, with how many
  songs you have together. Ticking one emails them an invitation to this song.
  They accept it from their notifications. Until they do, the
  invitation shows under Collaborators as **Invited**, with a **Cancel** button.

Pick **+ New Collaborator** and confirm, and the app generates a code.

Web app:
On the web, a code appears as a card under Collaborators. It has a copy button, **Share
Invite Link** and **Copy link**. Several people can be invited at once, and each
gets their own numbered code.

**Share Invite Link** hands it to any messaging app you like. The code on its
own works too, if you would rather read it down the phone.

Each code can only be used once. Inviting two people means generating two
codes.
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

heading: Joining a song
text:
The person you invited goes to **Settings**, then **Song Invite Code**.

Web app:
On the web there are several ways to the same **Join a Song** box:

- **Join with code** at the top of the **Songs** page, or press `J` there.
- **Got a code from a co-writer?** on [Home](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/tabs/home/), shown until you
  have a shared song. Click **Join a song**.
- **Joining a co-writer? Enter their code**, under the choices on the last step
  of the welcome a new account sees.
- **Join a song with a code** in the command palette (`⌘` `K` or `Ctrl` `K`).
- **Settings**, then **Join a Song**.

Type the code and the invitation appears once you have entered all six
characters, showing who invited you. Click **Join Song** to accept.
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

heading: Opening an invite link
text:
An invite link (`lyricgenie.app/invite?...`) opens a small page that asks where
you want to open the song, and shows the invite code.

- **On an iPhone or iPad**, choose **Open in the iPhone app** or **Continue on
  the web**.
- **On a computer**, choose **Open in your browser**. On a Mac, which can run
  the iPhone app, **Open in the Lyric Genie app** is offered too.

It is the same account either way. On the web, the code is already filled in,
so you only have to click **Join Song**. If you do not have the app yet, the
page links to the App Store.

Type the code, tap **Join Song**, and the song opens with both writers on it.
It also lands in their Songs list from then on.

Web app:
A person invited by email sees the invitation at the top of their notifications,
under **Invitations**, with **Accept** and **Decline**. See
[Notifications](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/notifications/).
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

heading: When a code is refused
text:
The person joining gets a specific message rather than a generic failure, and
each one means something different.

| What it says | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| **Invalid invite code format** | It is not six characters. Usually a typo or a missing character. |
| **Invite code not found or already used** | Codes are single use. Someone has already joined with it, or it was never real. |
| **This invite code has expired** | Codes do not last forever. Generate a fresh one. |
| **You're already a collaborator on this song** | They are on it. It will be in their Songs list. |
| **You must be signed in to use invite codes** | They opened the screen before signing in. |

In every case the fix is the same on your side: generate another code and send
it again. Nothing is consumed by a failed attempt.
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

heading: Who is on the song
text:
Back on the Collaborators screen you can see everyone.

Web app:
On the web it is the Collaborators section of the left panel, and a row of
avatars in the song bar shows who is in the song right now. Each writer has a
live status there, such as what section they are writing in. See
[Collaborator tabs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/tabs/#who-is-doing-what).

The **owner** is the person who made the song, marked with a star. Everyone
else has **Edit**, which lets them write, arrange, record and send lines.

Each co-writer is given a colour here, and it is the same colour their tab
carries in the editor. See
[Collaborator tabs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/tabs/).
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

heading: Removing someone
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Swipe left on their row. The app asks before it does anything.

Web app:
Only the song's owner can remove a co-writer. In the Collaborators section, open
the ⋯ beside their name and choose **Remove from song**. It asks first.

Removing a co-writer ends the collaboration for them. They keep a personal copy
of the song, so nothing they wrote is destroyed, but they no longer see your
version or anything you write in it afterwards.
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

heading: Stop sharing
text:
If you shared a song and nobody has joined it yet, you can make it a solo song
again. Only the owner can do this.

iPhone and iPad app:
Open the Collaborators screen, tap ⋯ at the top right, and choose **Stop
sharing**.

Web app:
Click the ⋯ button on the **Collaborators** section's header and choose **Stop
sharing**.

It asks first. Any invite codes nobody has used, and any email invitations still
waiting, stop working, and the Master tab goes away.

If the Master tab has lyrics on it, you choose what happens to them: **Add to
my lyrics** puts them in your lyrics, and **Move to scratchpad** puts them in
your scratchpad.

You can share the song again whenever you like. Once someone has joined,
**Stop sharing** is no longer offered.

**Stop sharing** needs the latest version of the iPhone app.
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

heading: Deleting a shared song
text:
You cannot. A song with collaborators on it refuses to be deleted, and archive
is offered instead. That is deliberate: deleting it would take the song away
from people who have been writing in it.

Web app:
The one exception is a shared song of yours that nobody has joined yet. Its ⋯
menu, in the song list or the song itself, offers **Stop Sharing & Delete** in
place of **Delete**. It asks first, then its invite codes and invitations stop
working and the song is deleted, for good.
description: Share a song with another writer using a one-time invite code. No email required, and it does not need Pro.

text:
Master is the version of the song you both agree on. It is not anybody's
personal tab, and it is not whatever the last person typed. Lines get put there
on purpose.

Every shared song has one, at the end of the tab row, in yellow.
description: The agreed version of a shared song, assembled deliberately from each writer's tab.

heading: You cannot type in Master
text:
This is the thing to understand before anything else. **Master is not editable.**
Tap the words and nothing happens: no cursor, no keyboard. There is no lamp
button on this tab either, so no Wish Workshop and no in-line suggestions.

Web app:
The same holds on the web: the Master tab is read-only, and the Wish and
Spark pill is not offered there.

Everything in Master arrived from somebody's tab, and the only things you can do
to it are reorder sections, delete them, or pull one back out.

That is deliberate. If Master could be typed into, it would become a fourth
draft competing with everyone else's, instead of the agreed version of the
other three.

To change a line, pull its section back to your own tab with **Send to Me**,
edit it there, and send it again. (On the web, **To Me** on the selection toolbar
does the same for the lines you have selected.)
description: The agreed version of a shared song, assembled deliberately from each writer's tab.

heading: Sending a section to Master
text:
From your own tab, open Arrange mode, select what you want, and choose
**Send to Master**. What happens next depends on what you selected.

Web app:
On the web you can also select text in the lyrics and click **To Master** on the
selection toolbar. It sends whole lines, so a partly selected line goes in
complete. You can send from your own tab, from a co-writer's tab and from the
Scratchpad, but not from the Master itself. After that it works as below.

**If you selected a whole named section**, header and all, the app already
knows what it is and files it silently. No prompt.

**If you selected loose lines**, it asks.

Types already in Master carry an **exists** label, so you can see what you are
about to collide with before you pick. A selection spanning several sections
asks once per section, with a count of how many are left.
description: The agreed version of a shared song, assembled deliberately from each writer's tab.

heading: When that section already exists
text:
- **Add as Chorus 2** keeps both and numbers them.
- **Replace Chorus** swaps the existing one out.
- **Cancel** abandons that section and moves to the next one waiting.
description: The agreed version of a shared song, assembled deliberately from each writer's tab.

heading: It files by section, not by arrival
text:
Master is not a pile in the order things turned up. Sections are held in song
order:

Intro, Verse, Pre-Chorus, Chorus, Hook, Post-Chorus, Bridge, Outro, then
anything custom.

In the figure above, the bridge was sent first and the chorus second. Master
still shows the chorus first, because that is where a chorus goes.
description: The agreed version of a shared song, assembled deliberately from each writer's tab.

heading: Reordering and removing
text:
The yellow button at the bottom right opens Master's own arrange mode. It works
in whole sections rather than individual lines, because Master is about
structure.

Web app:
On the web it is the **Arrange** pill in the song bar, as on any other tab. On
Master it works in whole sections: a checkbox sits on each header, clicking any
line selects its section, and there is no drag-to-reorder or Duplicate.

From there you can **Move Up** and **Move Down** to reorder, **Delete** a
section, or **Send to Me** to pull one back into your own tab to work on
privately.

Two people editing Master at the same time can collide. If someone else changes
it while you are working, the app stops and says **Conflict Detected** rather
than overwriting their version. Reopen the song and make your change again.
description: The agreed version of a shared song, assembled deliberately from each writer's tab.

heading: What reads from Master
text:
Master is what the rest of the app treats as the real song.

- **[Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/)** opens on Master by default when one exists.
- **[Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/)** default to Master, though you can
  pick any writer's tab instead.

Put something in Master early, even if it is only the chorus. It gives both of
you a shared reference point, and it makes Perform and lyric sheets useful
straight away.
description: The agreed version of a shared song, assembled deliberately from each writer's tab.

text:
The bell on the Start tab collects everything that happened while you were not
looking. A red dot means something is waiting.

Web app:
On the web the bell is in the app's top bar. Click it and the list opens over
the page. Everything shown is marked read a few seconds after you open it.
description: What Lyric Genie tells you about, and where those messages live once you have missed them.

heading: What is in there
text:
Notifications are grouped, and the groups appear in this order.

| Group | What lands in it |
| --- | --- |
| **Invitations** | Someone asking you onto a song. |
| **Activity** | What your co-writers did. |
| **Reminders** | Nudges to pick a song back up. |
| **Offers** | Occasional offers on Pro. |

Web app:
The web shows all four groups. An offer cannot be redeemed there: opening one
tells you to redeem it in the iOS app.
description: What Lyric Genie tells you about, and where those messages live once you have missed them.

heading: Collaboration events
text:
Most of what you see comes from shared songs.

- Someone **joined your song** after accepting an invitation.
- A co-writer **changed their lyrics**.
- A co-writer **sent you lines**. See
  [Sending lines to a co-writer](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/).
- Someone **changed the title**, or the mood, theme and similar artists.
- A co-writer **added a recording**. Opening it shows the song's recordings
  with that take highlighted.
- A co-writer sent a **new message** in a song's
  [chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/), while you were not in the song. Opening it
  opens the chat.
- (web) (coming soon) A co-writer **started a session** on a song. Opening it takes you
  to the session's camera and microphone check. See
  [Sessions](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sessions/).
- A collaboration **ended**, because you were removed, you left, or the owner
  deleted their account. You keep a personal copy either way, and the message
  says so.
description: What Lyric Genie tells you about, and where those messages live once you have missed them.

heading: News from Lyric Genie
text:
Now and then an announcement from us, such as a new feature, appears among your
**Activity** with a megaphone icon. Click or tap it to open the page it links
to. Announcements only go to people who have **Email Updates** switched on in
[Preferences](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/preferences/).
description: What Lyric Genie tells you about, and where those messages live once you have missed them.

heading: Reminders
text:
Two kinds arrive on their own.

**Keep writing.** A song you left unfinished, usually with a suggestion
attached, like adding a chorus or a bridge with Wish Workshop.

**Turn a recording into a song.** A voice memo you captured and have not done
anything with yet, with its title and length.
description: What Lyric Genie tells you about, and where those messages live once you have missed them.

heading: Clearing them
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Swipe left on anything to dismiss it. On an invitation, swiping left declines
it and swiping right accepts it, so you can deal with one without opening it.

Web app:
Hover a notification and click the small cross to dismiss it. An invitation has
**Accept** and **Decline** buttons.

**Dismiss All** empties the list. It does not undo anything, it only clears the
messages.

Accepting an invitation from here does the same thing as entering an invite
code. Either way the song appears in your Songs list and you get your own tab
in it.
description: What Lyric Genie tells you about, and where those messages live once you have missed them.

heading: Turning them off
text:
Push notifications are a system permission, so they live in the iOS Settings
app under Lyric Genie. Email is separate and lives in
[Preferences](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/account/preferences/), where **Email Updates** and
**Monthly Recap** can each be switched off. (iPhone and iPad)

Web app:
The web app has no push notifications. The bell is where these messages appear
while the app is open.
description: What Lyric Genie tells you about, and where those messages live once you have missed them.

text:
Your tab is yours alone, so getting a line from your tab into a co-writer's
means sending it. They decide whether to take it.

That is the whole design. Nothing lands in anybody's lyrics without them
agreeing to it.
description: Move lyrics between writers on a shared song. Lines you send arrive in the song's chat, and nothing lands in someone's tab until they add it.

heading: Sending
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Open Arrange mode, the grid button at the bottom right, and select the lines
you want. Tapping a section header takes the whole stanza.

iPhone and iPad app:
**Send to Collaborator** asks who should get them.

You can also select lines in the lyrics and choose **Send to** in the menu on
the selection, then **Send to Co-writer…**.

Web app:
Select the lines and click **Send to…** on the floating toolbar. With one
co-writer on the song, the lines go to them straight away. With more, a list asks
who should get them: tick one or several and click **Send**.

**Send to…** sends whole lines, widening your selection to the start and end of
each line.

On someone else's tab, **Send to Me** (**To Me** on the web) pulls their lines
into your own tab instead. Same idea, other direction.
description: Move lyrics between writers on a shared song. Lines you send arrive in the song's chat, and nothing lands in someone's tab until they add it.

heading: Where sent lines arrive
text:
Lines you are sent arrive in the song's [chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/) as a card
showing who sent them and the lines themselves. Long ones fold after four lines,
with **Show all** to read the rest.

- **Add to my lyrics** puts them at the end of your tab.
- **Decline** turns them down, and the sender sees that it was declined.

iPhone and iPad app:
**Add to my lyrics** also switches to your tab and turns on
[Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/), so you can move the new lines into place.

Lines waiting for you count toward the red number on the chat, so they are hard
to miss.

Older versions of the iPhone app keep sent lines in a separate Mailbox, the
button in the editor toolbar, with **Accept** and **Decline**. The
latest version moves them into the chat.
description: Move lyrics between writers on a shared song. Lines you send arrive in the song's chat, and nothing lands in someone's tab until they add it.

heading: Keeping track of what you sent
text:
Lines you sent show in the chat on your side too, as **You sent 4 lines to
Sam**, with what happened to them:

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Waiting** | They have not answered yet. |
| **Added** | It is in their tab. |
| **Declined** | They passed. |
| **Expired** | It sat too long. |
description: Move lyrics between writers on a shared song. Lines you send arrive in the song's chat, and nothing lands in someone's tab until they add it.

heading: Sending to the agreed version instead
text:
**Send to Master** (**To Master** on the web) skips all this and puts the lines
straight into the shared version. Nobody has to accept it, because Master is the
song rather than anyone's personal tab. See [The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/).
description: Move lyrics between writers on a shared song. Lines you send arrive in the song's chat, and nothing lands in someone's tab until they add it.

text:
A session is a live video call inside a song. Everyone in it sees and hears
each other while the lyrics stay on the page, so you can talk a line through,
play a part, or listen to a demo together without a separate call app.

Sessions are for the people writing the song. Only the song's writers can join
its session, and each song has one session at a time.

(coming soon)

Sessions are coming soon. A small group of writers is testing them now, and
this page describes how they work. Until they open to everyone, you won't see a
**Session** circle on Home or a **Session** section in a shared song.

Pro:
Starting a session is part of Pro, and a free trial counts. Joining is free:
while a Pro writer is in the session, any writer on the song can join, and
everyone in it can share their DAW, share computer audio and record. Without Pro,
the Session section shows **Join session** when a co-writer is in one, and
**Start a free trial** when nobody is. If every Pro writer has left, new writers
without Pro can't join until one is back.
description: See and hear your co-writers live while you write a song together, share your DAW or computer audio, and record the session to the song.
platformNote: Sessions are on the web app only for now. They are not on the iPhone app yet. Open the song at app.lyricgenie.app in a browser to start or join one.

heading: Starting a session
text:
There are two ways in.

### From Home

Click the green **Session** circle in Home's quick start. It opens the session
page, which has three parts:

- **The camera and mic check.** A preview of your camera, a level meter for
  your microphone, and menus to choose which **Microphone** and **Camera** to
  use. The two round buttons on the preview turn your mic and camera on or off
  before you go in.
- **The song.** By default a session starts a **New song**. Type a title, or
  leave it and the song is called "Session" with today's date. **Choose an
  existing song instead** lets you search your library and pick one. If a
  co-writer is already in a session on one of your songs, that song is picked
  for you and marked **Live now**.
- **Invite collaborators.** Optional. See [Inviting people](#inviting-people).

Click **Start session** when you are ready. The page takes you into the song
with the session running. If a co-writer is already in it, the button reads
**Join session**.

A session needs a shared song. Starting one on a new song, or on a song that is
just yours so far, shares it at that moment. The song then grows a
[Collaborators](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/) section and
[writer tabs](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/tabs/), the same as any shared song.

Headphones help. Without them your speakers can feed back into your mic. See
[There is an echo](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/troubleshooting/#there-is-an-echo).

### Inside a song

On a shared song, **Session** is a section of the left panel, between
**Collaborators** and **Chat**. It also has an icon in the column of icons on
the left edge of the window.

Click **Start a session** in that section. A smaller check opens with just your
camera and mic, and **Start session**.

The check has a box underneath: **Skip this check next time (join with these
settings)**. Tick it and later sessions in this browser start straight away,
with the same mic and camera choices. To check them again, click **Check
camera and mic first** under the start button.

A solo song has no Session section. Start the session from Home and choose the
song there, or [invite someone](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/) first.
description: See and hear your co-writers live while you write a song together, share your DAW or computer audio, and record the session to the song.
platformNote: Sessions are on the web app only for now. They are not on the iPhone app yet. Open the song at app.lyricgenie.app in a browser to start or join one.

heading: Inviting people
text:
On the session page from Home, **Invite collaborators** gives you two ways to
bring people in:

- **Email.** People you have written songs with before are listed with their
  email and how many songs you share. Tick the ones you want. When you click
  **Start session**, they get an email saying you are starting a session, with
  a link to join.
- **Code.** **New collaborator** makes an invite code to send to anyone, however
  you like. Each code works once, so make one per person with **Another new
  collaborator**. Whoever uses a code joins the song as a co-writer.

While you are alone in a session, a **Waiting for co-writers** strip shows who
you invited, and **Copy invite link** copies a link to send.

Inside a song, invite people the usual way, from the **Collaborators** section.
See [Inviting a co-writer](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/inviting/).
description: See and hear your co-writers live while you write a song together, share your DAW or computer audio, and record the session to the song.
platformNote: Sessions are on the web app only for now. They are not on the iPhone app yet. Open the song at app.lyricgenie.app in a browser to start or join one.

heading: Joining a session
text:
When a co-writer starts a session, you find out in three places.

- **The bell.** The song's other writers get a **started a session**
  notification. Clicking it opens the camera and mic check for that song, then
  takes you in. Co-writers are told at most once every half hour per song.
- **The song.** If you open a song while co-writers are in its session, a green
  banner over the lyrics says who, for example **Sam is in a session** on this
  song. Click **Join**. The × hides the banner for this visit. The Session
  section and its icon on the left also show a green **Live** dot.
- **Home.** The **Session** circle shows that a co-writer is live on one of
  your recent shared songs.

The song's chat marks the moment each person joins or leaves, as a small line
such as **Sam joined the session** with the time.

If you were invited by email from a session page, accepting the invitation on
the web takes you to that song's session check.
description: See and hear your co-writers live while you write a song together, share your DAW or computer audio, and record the session to the song.
platformNote: Sessions are on the web app only for now. They are not on the iPhone app yet. Open the song at app.lyricgenie.app in a browser to start or join one.

heading: The session view
text:
### In the left panel

While you are in a session, the Session section shows everyone's video, the
**Audio inputs** list, and a row of round buttons. A coloured ring around a
video means that person is talking.

Drag the bar under the video to make it taller or shorter. Double-click the bar
to put it back.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Microphone | Mutes and unmutes you. |
| Camera | Turns your camera off and on. |
| Headphones | Music mode. See [below](#music-mode). |
| Sliders | Adds an audio input. See [Audio inputs](#audio-inputs). |
| Screen | Shares your screen. See [Sharing your screen](#sharing-your-screen). |
| Record | Records the session. See [Recording a session](#recording-a-session). |
| Pop out | Puts the session in its own window. See [Pop out](#pop-out). |
| **Leave** | Leaves the session. |

### The expanded view

The expand button on the Session header, or the Session icon on the left edge,
opens the session at full size. Videos are as large as the space allows.

- **Click a video** to make it large, with the others small underneath. **Tile
  view**, the grid button in its corner, goes back.
- **The chat button** in the Session header shows the song's chat as a column
  beside the video. It starts hidden, and the app remembers your choice. A red
  dot on it means unread messages. Drag the line between the video and the
  chat to resize them, and double-click it to reset.

### Sharing your screen

Click the screen button and your browser asks what to share: a window, a tab,
or the whole screen. Everyone sees it as its own tile, next to your camera.
When a co-writer starts sharing, their screen comes up large in the expanded
view. Click the button again to stop.

Screen sharing works on a computer. Phones and tablets cannot share a screen
from the browser.

### Pop out

In Chrome and Edge on a computer, the pop-out button moves the session into a
small window that stays on top of other apps. That keeps your co-writers in
view while you work in a DAW. The panel says **Session is in its own window**.
Click **Bring back** to return it. In other browsers the button is not there.

### On a phone

On a phone, your co-writers' video sits in a bar along the bottom of the song,
above the toolbar, with buttons to mute, turn your camera off, add audio,
record and leave. Tap a video to open the full session view. The arrow at the
end hides the bar to a small **Session · Show** pill. In the full view the chat
sits below the video instead of beside it.

heading: Audio inputs
text:
**Audio inputs** lists every sound source in the session, each with a live
meter. Your own come first, then your co-writers'. Click the heading to fold it
away.

### Your microphone

The first row is your mic, with the device's name. The small arrow beside it
switches to another microphone.

Your mic has echo cancellation and noise reduction, which suits talking.

### Music mode

The headphones button turns on music mode, for singing or playing an instrument
into your mic. It turns off echo cancellation and noise reduction so the sound
comes through as it is. The app asks you to put on headphones first, because
without them your speakers feed straight back into your mic. Click the button
again to turn music mode off.

### Adding audio

**Add audio input**, under your rows, or the sliders button, opens a menu of
other things you can share. Anything shared this way goes out clearly, without
the voice processing your mic gets.

- **Your DAW.** Live audio from your DAW through the Lyric Genie Session plugin.
  See [Share your DAW live](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/guides/daw-plugin/).
- **Computer audio (a tab or your screen).** Your browser asks what to share.
  In Chrome and Edge, turn on **Share audio** in that window, or no sound comes
  through. Safari cannot share computer audio this way. Use an audio device
  instead.
- **Audio devices.** An audio interface, or a virtual device such as BlackHole
  or Loopback that your DAW plays into. A device sends its first two channels,
  so choose which inputs feed them in the device's own mixer. Your current
  microphone is left off this list, so you are never heard twice.

You can share up to three audio inputs at once, as well as your mic. Remove one
to add another.

### Levels

Each row has a meter, a volume slider and a mute button. What they do depends
on whose row it is.

| Row | Slider | Mute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yours | How loud it is **for everyone**. 100% sends it as it is; you can go up to 150% for a quiet source. | Mutes it for everyone. It stays shared. |
| A co-writer's | How loud you hear it. Only you. | Mutes it for you only. |

Point at a slider to see its percentage. Your own extra inputs also have an ×
to stop sharing them.

The meter is green, turns yellow in the last 3 dB, and shows red when a peak
reaches the top. If your source keeps hitting red, turn its slider down.

heading: Recording a session
text:
Click the record button to record the session. It records what you hear: your
mic, your co-writers' mics, and every shared source, mixed together.

While it records, the button turns red and shows the time. Click it to stop.
The recording saves to the song's [Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/recordings/) as
**Session recording** followed by the time it started, and **Saved · Show**
takes you to it. Your co-writers get the usual notification that a recording
was added.

Everyone in the session is told when recording starts and stops, whoever starts
it. They hear a chime, see a short notice, and a red banner stays at the top of
the session saying who is recording, for example **Sam is recording this
session**. On a phone the bar shows a red **Rec** pill. Joining a session that
is already being recorded tells you so.

A session recording can be up to {{limit.recording.proPerItem}} long. The button
turns amber in the last five minutes, and the recording stops and saves itself
at the limit. Leaving the session while recording also saves what you have.

heading: Connection quality
text:
If your connection is weak, the session says **Your connection is weak. Audio
comes first; video may stutter.** A co-writer with a weak connection shows a
**Weak** label on their video.

If it stays weak for a few seconds, the app pauses the video coming in to you
so the audio stays smooth. Co-writers show their picture instead of a frozen
frame. **Turn video back on** brings it back. Video also comes back by itself
once your connection has been good for a while.

If the connection drops, the session shows **Reconnecting…** and carries on when
it can.
description: See and hear your co-writers live while you write a song together, share your DAW or computer audio, and record the session to the song.

heading: Leaving and ending
text:
Click **Leave** to leave. Leaving the song, or closing the tab, also takes you
out of the session. A session ends when the last person leaves. Nothing about
the song changes, and your co-writers can start a new one at any time.

So a session left open by mistake does not run on for hours, the app ends it
for you:

- **Alone.** If you are the only one in the session for 10 minutes, you leave
  it, with a note saying why.
- **Quiet.** After about an hour and a half with nobody talking, nothing
  shared, and no typing or clicking, the app asks **Still in the session?** and counts down a
  minute. Click **Stay** to keep going, or **Leave now**.
- **Very long.** After about four hours the same question appears, however busy
  the session is.

Talking, playing, or sharing audio counts as staying, so a session with music
playing from your DAW is not cut off while you work in another app.

text:
Share a song and the editor grows a row of tabs. Each writer gets one, and
everyone can see everyone else's.

Nobody types over anybody. You write in your tab, they write in theirs, and the
version you both agree on is assembled deliberately in a third one.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: Reading the tabs
text:
Web app:
On the web the tab row sits above the lyrics, and a green dot on a tab means
that writer is in the song right now. It dims when they have left. The
Collaborators section of the left panel says what each writer is doing. See
[Who is doing what](#who-is-doing-what).

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Your name (You)** | Your own tab. The only one you can type in. |
| A star beside a name | That writer owns the song. |
| A filled dot | They are in the song right now. |
| An outlined dot | They are not. |
| **Master** | The agreed version. See [The Master](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/master/). |

Colours are assigned, not chosen. The owner is purple and everyone else takes
the next colour in the list, which is the same colour shown against their name
on the Collaborators screen.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: Watching a co-writer write
text:
Open a co-writer's tab while they are in the song and you see their cursor as
it moves: a line in their colour with their first name on it. When they select
text, the selection shows in their colour too. It all happens live, so you can
follow along as they write without either of you saving or refreshing.

Live cursors need the latest version of the iPhone app.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: Who is doing what
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The Collaborators screen lists everyone on the song, each in their tab colour,
with a status under their name. A green dot means they are in the song now.

Web app:
The **Collaborators** section of the left panel lists everyone on the song,
each in their tab colour, with a status under their name. On a computer, the
**Collaborators** icon at the top of the column of icons on the left edge opens
it on its own. A co-writer's row has an **Open tab** button that switches to
their tab.

| Status | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Writing in** a section, such as **Writing in Verse 1** | Typing in their own tab. |
| **Here · in** a section, or **Here now** | In the song, with their cursor in that section, but not typing. |
| **Recording…** | Recording a take. |
| **Uploading audio…** | Adding an audio file. |
| **Typing in chat…** | Writing a message in the [chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/). |
| **Performing** | In [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/). |
| **Arranging** | In [Arrange mode](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/arrange-mode/). |
| **Looking at your tab**, **Looking at the Master**, or **Looking at** someone's tab | Reading a tab other than their own. |
| **Last edited** and a time | Not in the song. They were the last to change it. |
| **Owner** or **Co-writer** | Not in the song. |

Web app:
Writers who are not in the song right now look slightly faded, with no green
dot.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: What is yours and what is shared
text:
**Your tab is yours.** Co-writers can read it but cannot edit it. To get your
words into someone else's hands you send them, which is covered in
[Sending lines to a co-writer](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/).

**Section headers take your colour.** Write a Bridge in your tab and the header
is your colour rather than the app's purple, so a glance at a tab tells you
whose work it is.

**The Scratchpad stays private.** Nobody else can see it, on any song. It is
the right place for a line you are not ready to show.

Web app:
On a shared song the scratchpad says **Private · only you can see this**. Each
writer has their own. Songs shared before this worked this way had one set of
scratchpad notes for everyone, and those notes were copied into each writer's
private scratchpad, so nobody lost anything. The iOS app does the same from
version 2.21.

**Recordings are shared.** Audio attached to the song is visible to everyone on
it.

iPhone and iPad app:
Each tab shows the takes belonging to that writer as a strip of
chips. When a writer has more takes than fit, the strip
ends in a **⋯ +3**.

Tap a chip and a small player appears without leaving the tab, with skip back,
play and pause, skip forward, and a close button. You can listen to how a
co-writer sang their verse while reading the words they wrote for it, which is
the point of putting the two side by side.

Web app:
On the web, a take linked to lyrics shows as a bar beside those lines in that
writer's tab, and clicking it plays it in the player pinned below the editor.
The Recordings section of the left panel lists every take on the song. See
[Recordings](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/recordings/).
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: What changes in the toolbar
text:
A shared song adds a way to talk to your co-writers.

- (iPhone and iPad) The **Chat** button appears on the right of the editor toolbar,
  with a red number when there is something new. See
  [Co-writer chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/).
- (iPhone and iPad) **Collaborators** moves off the toolbar and into the ⋯ menu.
- (web) **Collaborators** and **Chat** move to the top of the left panel,
  and the selection toolbar gains **To Master**, **Send to…**, and **To Me** on
  someone else's tab. See [Sending lines](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/sending/) and
  [Co-writer chat](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/collaboration/chat/).
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: Side by side (web)
text:
Web app:
On a computer you can read a co-writer's tab, or the Master, next to your own.
Choose **View**, then **Side by side**, or right-click a writer's tab and
choose **Open side by side**.

- **Your tab stays on the left**, and you can keep writing in it.
- **The right side shows another tab**, read-only. It has its own row of tabs,
  so you can switch between co-writers and the Master there. The × closes it.
- **Drag the divider** between them to give one side more room.
  Double-click it to make them even again.
- **Each side scrolls on its own**, so you can line up your verse with theirs.

The song remembers whether it was side by side, and what was on the right, the
next time you open it.

You can select text on the right just as on any co-writer's tab: look up rhymes
or synonyms, **Ask Genie**, send lines **To Me** or **To Master**, or link the
lines to a recording.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

heading: If you are removed, or you leave
text:
You keep a personal copy of the song under a new title, so nothing you wrote is
lost. You stop seeing the shared version and anything written in it afterwards.
description: On a shared song every writer gets their own lyric tab in their own colour, plus a Master tab for the agreed version.

text:
AI Style is where you tell Lyric Genie how you want it to write, once, instead
of saying it again in every wish.

Everything here applies to the whole app rather than one song. Open it from the
⋯ menu in [the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/), or from Settings.

Web app:
On the web, AI Style is a section at the bottom of Settings, and it saves when
you click out of a field.
description: Standing instructions for the AI, including words you never want it to use.

heading: Style Guidance
text:
A free-form note about how you want suggestions written. Tone, perspective,
the things you lean into, the things you are tired of.

The app's own example is a good shape to copy:

> keep it conversational. no complex language. no weather metaphors.

Short and blunt works better than a paragraph of theory. You have 300
characters, and the counter turns red as you reach the end.

This is read by [Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) and by in-line
suggestions, so it shapes both the things you ask for and the things that
appear on their own.
description: Standing instructions for the AI, including words you never want it to use.

heading: Words to Avoid
text:
A list of words you do not want to see. Type a word and it becomes a tag;
tap the small cross on a tag to remove it.

Songwriters tend to fill this with their own tics, or with the words that
every AI reaches for. The app will still use one if it is genuinely the
strongest choice, so treat it as a strong preference rather than a ban.

The quickest way to find your list is to use Wish Workshop for a week and note
which word keeps turning up. That is the one to add.

The web app keeps your Style Guidance and Words to Avoid on your account, while
the iOS app keeps its own on each device. They are not shared, so set them up
once in each app you write in.
description: Standing instructions for the AI, including words you never want it to use.

heading: What it does not do
text:
AI Style is not per song. If you want to steer one song in particular, that is
what mood, theme and similar artists are for on
[the song editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/).

It is also not a filter applied after the fact. The guidance goes in before the
writing happens, so it shapes the suggestion rather than censoring it.
description: Standing instructions for the AI, including words you never want it to use.

text:
Sometimes you have two good versions of a line and you are not ready to choose.
Write both on the same line with a slash between them, and Lyric Genie keeps
the first as the line and the rest as alternates.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

heading: Writing an alternate
text:
Type a space, a slash and a space between the versions:

```
I left it all behind / I don't know why
```

The first version is the **main line**. Everything after a ` / ` is an
alternate. A line can hold more than one:

```
Out on the edge / Out on the wire / Out past the fire
```

The spaces matter. `24/7` and `and/or` have no spaces around the slash, so they
stay ordinary text. A section header such as `[Chorus]` never has alternates.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

heading: How alternates look
text:
The main line reads as normal. Each alternate is faded, and the slash before it
is coloured so you can see where one version ends and the next begins.

The text is stored exactly as you typed it. Nothing is hidden or moved, and you
edit an alternate like any other text.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

heading: Swapping in an alternate
text:
Web app:
Point at the line, or put your cursor on it, and a small ⇄ appears at the end of
each alternate. Click it and that alternate becomes the main line: it moves to
the front, and the old main line becomes the first alternate. **Undo** puts it back.

On a tab you can't edit, such as a co-writer's, the ⇄ is shown dimmed and does
nothing.

iPhone and iPad app:
Put your cursor on the line and a ⇄ button appears at its right edge. Tap it and
the first alternate becomes the main line, and the old main line takes its
place as the first alternate. Tap again to swap them back. Each swap is one step
of **Undo**.

The ⇄ only appears on a tab you can edit.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

heading: What reads only the main line
text:
Anything that has to treat the line as one line uses the main version and
ignores the alternates:

- [Lyric sheets](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/lyric-sheets/).
- Syllable counts, and the rhyme letters in the margin. See
  [Rhyme colors and margins](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/view-options/).
- Refine Context, and title suggestions.

iPhone and iPad app:
In the iPhone app, [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/) and
[Wish Workshop](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/wish-workshop/) also use the main line.

Web app:
On the web, [Perform](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/perform/) shows the line as you typed it, with
its alternates.

[Genie](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/genie/) sees every version on purpose, so you can ask it which
one works better.

Alternate lines need the latest version of the iPhone app. An older version
shows the line exactly as typed, slash and all, so nothing is lost.
description: Keep two or more versions of a lyric line side by side with a spaced slash, and swap which one is the main line with one click.

text:
Arrange mode turns your lyrics into a checklist. Instead of a cursor and a
keyboard you get a checkbox on every line, and a row of actions that move those
lines around.

It is for structure. Use it when the words are right but they are in the wrong
order, or when a verse needs to become two.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Getting in and out
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
The grid button at the bottom right of [the editor](https://lyricgenie.app/docs/editor/) opens it. The
same button turns into a house, and tapping that takes you back to writing.

Web app:
Click **Arrange** in the song bar. The pill turns into **Done**, and clicking
that takes you back to writing. On a phone browser, Arrange is in the bar along
the bottom of the editor.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Selecting
text:
iPhone and iPad app:
Tap any line to select it, and tap it again to let it go. The count in the
middle of the bottom bar tells you how many you have.

Web app:
Click a line or its checkbox to select it, and click again to let it go. The
actions sit in a bar along the bottom of the lyrics.

**Press and drag down the column of checkboxes** and every line you pass is
selected. It is much faster than tapping a run of lines one at a time, and it is
the fastest way to take a block that does not line up with a section.

Tapping a **section header** selects that header and every line under it. That
is the quick way to move a whole chorus, and it is the thing most people do not
discover on their own.

**Select All** takes the entire song, and becomes **Deselect All** once
everything is picked.
description: Reorder, duplicate and delete whole lines of a song without editing the words.

heading: Dragging a single line
text:
Web app:
Each line has a grip on its right. Drag the grip to pick that line up and drop
it somewhere else, without selecting anything or using the arrows. Unlike the
